worked_solution:
If we let $u=5-x,$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-1\,⟹\,-\,\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $4$ | $2$ |

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}3\cdot {2}^{5-x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{4}^{2}3\cdot {2}^{u}(-1)\text{d}u \\  & =-3{\int }_{4}^{2}{2}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-3(\frac{{2}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}){|}_{4}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}({2}^{2}-{2}^{4}) \\  & =-\frac{3}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(4-16) \\  & =\frac{36}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\end{aligned}
$$
